evidence.title: Nelson Bay Cave (South Africa): Holocene Later Stone Age coastal sequence
evidence.dateBasis: Bayesian radiocarbon age models on marine shell and charcoal across Albany-to-Wilton Later Stone Age strata.
evidence.summary: Deeply stratified coastal cave capturing shifting Holocene shellfish foraging, marine hunting, and backed microlith technologies along the southern Cape shoreline.
evidence.limits: Marine reservoir offsets require paired shell/terrestrial Bayesian modeling.

evidence.title: Tsodilo Hills (Botswana): Holocene rock art, forager-herder contact & mining
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified shelter sequences and Early Iron Age specularite/trade settlements (Divuyu & Nqoma) at Tsodilo.
evidence.summary: Preserves dense rock paintings alongside Kalahari Later Stone Age occupations followed by sixth–eleventh century Divuyu and Nqoma villages linked to regional cattle and specularite-iron exchange.
evidence.limits: Painted panel ages cannot be equated directly with floor deposit radiocarbon dates.

evidence.title: Lothagam North Pillar Site (Lake Turkana): Monumental pastoral cemetery
evidence.dateBasis: Direct AMS dates on human remains and stone pillar mortuary platform overlooking Lake Turkana.
evidence.summary: A communal megalithic platform cemetery holding over 500 individuals built during East Africa’s earliest livestock arrival, showing shared egalitarian monumentality across men, women, and children adorned with stone and ostrich eggshell beads.
evidence.limits: Preserved cemeteries near falling shoreline levels outnumber excavated contemporary herder camps.

evidence.title: Luxmanda (Tanzania): Southernmost Savanna Pastoral Neolithic settlement
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon dates, geophysical survey, and direct ancient genomes from Savanna Pastoral Neolithic contexts.
evidence.summary: A major planned Savanna Pastoral Neolithic settlement showing heavy reliance on cattle, sheep, goats, and sorghum/milk economies alongside admixed northeastern-eastern African pastoralist genomes.
evidence.limits: Geophysical features show spatial planning that remains only partially excavated.

evidence.title: Yeha (Tigray, Ethiopia): Pre-Aksumite monumental temple & settlement
evidence.dateBasis: Archaeological sequences at the Great Temple of Yeha, Grat Be’al Guebri, and northeast Tigray settlements.
evidence.summary: Monumental dry-stone temple and elite palace structures blending indigenous northern Horn cereal/teff farming and pottery with South Arabian (Sabaic) epigraphy and architectural idioms.
evidence.limits: Chronologies rely heavily on elite temple/palace trenches while surrounding rural villages are fewer.

evidence.title: Great Lakes Urewe & Kakapel Sequence: Early Iron Age & mixed crops
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified rockshelter macrobotanical dates (Kakapel), furnace dates, and Early Iron Age Urewe dimple-based pottery horizons.
evidence.summary: Marks early ironworking and beveled Urewe pottery around Lake Victoria where West, East, and Northeast African crops (cowpea, pearl millet, sorghum, finger millet) integrated alongside multilingual cultural syncretism.
evidence.limits: Coordinates cover a key Lake Victoria corridor rather than all regional Early Iron Age smelting centers.

evidence.title: Leopard Cave (Erongo, Namibia): Early southern caprine introduction
evidence.dateBasis: Directly AMS-dated sheep remains in Later Stone Age stratigraphy.
evidence.summary: Supplies some of the earliest directly dated domesticated sheep bones in southwestern Africa, showing domesticates appearing among forager–herder frontiers along western routes.
evidence.limits: Direct dates on single caprine elements highlight small initial herd presence rather than full pastoral transformation.

evidence.title: Adulis (Zula Bay, Eritrea): Red Sea emporium of Aksum
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated harbor architecture, Ayla-Aksum amphorae, coins, and Byzantine churches on the Eritrean Red Sea coast.
evidence.summary: Aksum’s principal maritime gateway linking Ethiopian highland ivory, gold, obsidian, and frankincense with Roman-Byzantine Egypt, South Arabia, and western Indian Ocean shipping lanes.
evidence.limits: Alluvial fan silting buried early waterfront wharves beneath thick marine-fluvial deposits.

evidence.title: Aksum & Bieta Giyorgis (Ethiopia): Highland capital & carved stelae
evidence.dateLabel: c. 50–750 CE (Ona roots earlier from ~360 BCE)
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified excavations on Bieta Giyorgis hill, royal monolith quarries, coin series, and Ge’ez/Greek inscriptions.
evidence.summary: Imperial highland capital famous for towering monolithic granite stelae, Aksumite gold/silver/bronze coinage, multi-story palaces, rainwater cisterns, and early Christian state adoption in the fourth century CE.
evidence.limits: Post-7th century transition outside the monumental core remains under-excavated.

evidence.title: Beta Samati (Northern Tigray): Aksumite trade & basilica town
evidence.dateBasis: Bayesian AMS radiocarbon model through Pre-Aksumite to Late Aksumite domestic, basilica, and gold-intaglio ring contexts.
evidence.summary: Excavations uncovered a long-lived highland town bridging Pre-Aksumite and Aksumite eras, hosting an early fourth-century Christian basilica alongside mixed Christian-Aksumite seals and imported Red Sea amphorae.
evidence.limits: Represents a single excavated regional administrative hub northeast of Aksum.

evidence.title: Kasteelberg (Western Cape, South Africa): Coastal Khoekhoe pastoralists
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified granite-hilltop Kasteelberg excavations and coastal shell-midden pastoralist radiocarbon chronologies.
evidence.summary: Granite kopje camps along South Africa’s West Coast preserving early ceramic-using sheep and cattle herders alongside intense coastal Cape fur seal harvesting.
evidence.limits: Fine resolution separates distinct intermittent herder visits rather than permanent village walls.

evidence.title: Unguja Ukuu (Zanzibar): First-millennium Swahili-Indian Ocean port
evidence.dateBasis: Magnetometry surveys, stratified earth-and-thatch house trenches, and direct crop AMS dates (rice, cotton, mung bean).
evidence.summary: Reveals an expansive early urban beach port of timber-and-daub architecture trading Tana Tradition local wares alongside Persian Gulf Siraf ceramics, Sasanian-Islamic wares, and Asian crops.
evidence.limits: Coastal compaction and medieval looting/reworking affect later layers.

evidence.title: Bosutswe (eastern Botswana): Long Iron Age Kalahari-margin town
evidence.dateBasis: Six-meter stratified hilltop sequence bridging Toutswe, Mapungubwe, and Zimbabwe-era trade.
evidence.summary: Hilltop town overlooking the Kalahari fringe that linked cattle wealth, copper metallurgy, and specularite/ivory hunting to Indian Ocean glass-bead trade networks.
evidence.limits: Hilltop stratigraphy reflects both domestic housing and livestock kraals shifting through phases.

evidence.title: Dembeni & Comoros Corridor: Early Austronesian–African maritime contact
evidence.dateBasis: Direct radiocarbon dates on Asian crop assemblages (rice, mung bean) and regional Comorian–Swahili admixture genetics.
evidence.summary: Situated across the northern Mozambique Channel, Dembeni preserves Swahili/Dembeni pottery alongside the earliest archaeological Asian rice and mung beans in the western Indian Ocean, corroborated by genetic admixture dating.
evidence.limits: Genetic admixture estimates carry broad generation-time uncertainty alongside sharper botanical AMS dates.

evidence.title: Mahilaka & NW Madagascar: Early urban port & mixed Island settlement
evidence.dateLabel: c. 850–1400 CE (Main urban port c. 1000–1400 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated stone-walled town sectors, chloritic-schist vessels, botanical crops, and island-wide genomic sampling.
evidence.summary: One of Madagascar’s earliest urban trading towns, surrounded by monumental stone walls and mosques while inland and coastal communities combined Austronesian and East African Bantu genetic and linguistic legacies.
evidence.limits: Exact timing and number of founding oceanic crossings before 900 CE remain actively debated.

evidence.title: Kilwa Kisiwani & Songo Mnara (Tanzania): Coral-stone Swahili city-state
evidence.dateLabel: c. 800–1505 CE (Peak coral architecture c. 1300–1500; Portuguese fort 1505)
evidence.dateBasis: Excavations at the Great Mosque, Husuni Kubwa palace, minted Kilwa coinage, and Songo Mnara town surveys.
evidence.summary: Southern Swahili island metropolis that minted copper/silver/gold coins, built the domed Great Mosque and clifftop Husuni Kubwa palace out of Porites coral limestone, and brokered Zimbabwe Plateau gold until Portuguese seizure and fortification in 1505.
evidence.limits: Intertidal sea erosion increasingly threatens outlying reefs, causeways, and stone mosques.

evidence.title: Gedi & Mida Creek (Kenya): Coral-stone Swahili town & outports
evidence.dateBasis: Walled coral-rag palace/mosque sequences and outport creek surveys along coastal central Kenya.
evidence.summary: A major inland forest Swahili stone town enclosed by nested walls with a Friday Mosque, royal palace, pillar tombs, Chinese porcelain imports, and mangrove-creek outport links.
evidence.limits: Abandonment causes in the seventeenth century likely combined shifting Indian Ocean trade, regional conflict, and water-table changes.

evidence.title: Chwaka (Pemba Island): Swahili townlands & coral mosques
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified sequence of four successive coral-lime mosques amidst dense wattle-and-daub domestic neighborhoods.
evidence.summary: Shows how earthen-and-timber residential neighborhoods anchored Swahili townlands around monumental coral mosques, demonstrating civic Islamic urban life beyond rare stone mansions.
evidence.limits: Perishable wattle-and-daub architecture leaves subtle geophysical and posthole footprints.

evidence.title: Schroda, K2 & Mapungubwe Hill (Limpopo Valley): Early Southern African state
evidence.dateBasis: Extensive AMS radiocarbon dates from Schroda, K2 mounds, and royal gold-burial graves atop Mapungubwe Hill.
evidence.summary: Chronicles rapid class stratification in the Shashe-Limpopo Basin—moving from ivory/glass-bead exchange at Schroda and K2 to sacred hilltop kingship, dry-stone terrace walls, and goldsmithing at Mapungubwe.
evidence.limits: Debates continue over Mapungubwe’s chronological overlap with Mapela Hill and early Great Zimbabwe.

evidence.title: Mapela Hill (southwestern Zimbabwe): Contested early Zimbabwe urbanism
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon-dated dry-stone terraced hillside platforms and Zhizo/K2-to-Zimbabwe ceramics.
evidence.summary: Documents extensive stone-walled prestige terracing and exotic glass beads roughly contemporaneous with K2–Mapungubwe, supporting polycentric rather than single-site models of Zimbabwe-culture state formation.
evidence.limits: Extent of early eleventh-century stone walling versus later terraces remains actively studied.

evidence.title: Great Zimbabwe (Masvingo): Monumental capital of the Zimbabwe plateau
evidence.dateBasis: Bayesian modeling of all radiocarbon determinations alongside revised AMS dates on Hill Complex, Valley Enclosures, and Great Enclosure.
evidence.summary: Largest dry-stone granite urban complex south of the Zambezi, integrating commoner dhaka house compounds with towering Hill and Conical Tower enclosures, gold-smelting crucibles, Zimbabwe soapstone birds, and Indian Ocean porcelain.
evidence.limits: Early nineteenth-century antiquarian looting stripped key upper floors of the Great Enclosure.

evidence.title: Lalibela (Lasta, Ethiopia): Monolithic rock-hewn church capital
evidence.dateBasis: Geomorphological quarry analysis, trench excavations around Bete Gabriel–Rufael, and Zagwe–early Solomonic historiography.
evidence.summary: Eleven interconnected monolithic and semi-monolithic churches carved downward out of volcanic tuff linked by subterranean trenches, drainage cisterns, and a surrounding medieval highland urban landscape.
evidence.limits: Direct carving dates of individual rock-cut churches remain difficult relative to excavated spoil trenches.

evidence.title: Ntusi & Bigo bya Mugenyi (western Uganda): Great Lakes earthwork capitals
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon sequences from Ntusi ash/bone middens and kilometres of deep defensive-symbolic trenches at Bigo.
evidence.summary: Shows centralized pastoral-agrarian polities in the western Ugandan grasslands mobilizing massive labor to dig multi-kilometre earthen ditch systems and stock-handling enclosures alongside salt and iron networks.
evidence.limits: Attribution of Bigo specifically to named Cwezi oral traditions remains an archaeological hypothesis.

evidence.title: Engaruka (Northern Tanzania): Terraced stone-lined irrigation fields
evidence.dateBasis: Geoarchaeological soil micromorphology, radiocarbon determinations, and Rift Valley escarpment field-channel mapping.
evidence.summary: Engineered stone-lined canal networks fed roughly 2,000 hectares of terraced sorghum fields below densely nucleated stone-platform hillside villages before climate-and-discharge shifts spurred abandonment.
evidence.limits: Population estimates vary significantly based on house-platform contemporaneity assumptions.

evidence.title: Khami (Southwestern Zimbabwe): Successor capital of the Torwa-Butua state
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon chronology, terraced granite retaining walls, Chinese Ming/European imports, and regional Khami-phase surveys.
evidence.summary: Flourished after Great Zimbabwe’s decline, replacing free-standing enclosures with checkered and herringbone retaining stone walls supporting elevated royal mud houses, household workshops, and regional cattle-gold exchange.
evidence.limits: Links between Torwa and later Rozvi Changamire phases continue to be refined by AMS dating.

evidence.title: Bokoni (Mpumalanga, South Africa): Contoured agricultural stone terraces
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon determinations from Komati Gorge Village 1 paired with 150 km belt landscape mapping and phytolith soils.
evidence.summary: Integrated thousands of terraced agricultural hillsides, walled cattle tracks, and circular homesteads across an intensive highveld farming belt disrupted by early nineteenth-century regional warfare.
evidence.limits: Directly excavated radiocarbon dates remain concentrated in select valleys such as Komati Gorge.

evidence.title: Gondar (Fasil Ghebbi, Ethiopia): Solomonic imperial stone capital
evidence.dateBasis: Royal Ethiopian chronicles, dated lime-mortar palace phases (Fasiladas through Iyasu II), and heritage structural surveys.
evidence.summary: Permanent highland stone capital established by Emperor Fasiladas around a walled compound of multi-story basalt-and-lime palaces, churches, baths, and multi-confessional quarters integrating regional Christian, Muslim, and Beta Israel artisan towns.
evidence.limits: Colonial-era conflicts and twentieth-century weathering altered portions of the castle complex.

evidence.title: Highland Madagascar & Ambohimanga: Fortified hills & Merina polity
evidence.dateBasis: Central Highlands ditch-ringed rova hillfort surveys, irrigated rice-terrace studies, and Merina royal history up to French colonial conquest in 1895–1896.
evidence.summary: Ditch-enclosed royal hilltops like Ambohimanga united surrounding terraced rice plains into the centralized Kingdom of Madagascar (Imerina), developing metallurgy, diplomatic alliances, and fortified resistance until French annexation in 1896.
evidence.limits: Highland sequences complement distinct coastal and southern Antandroy regional histories.

evidence.title: Panga ya Saidi (Coastal Kenya): Later Stone Age forager-farmer interface
evidence.dateLabel: c. 8000 BCE–900 CE (Holocene LSA & Early Iron Age layers)
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified cave hearth sequence, ostrich-eggshell/marine beads, and coastal Iron Age Tana ceramics atop LSA layers.
evidence.summary: Coastal limestone upland cave recording persistent Holocene hunter-gatherer adaptation intersecting early farming, domestic fauna, and Tana Tradition coastal trade pottery into the late first millennium CE.
evidence.limits: Represents upland coastal forest margin interaction complementing shoreline Swahili ports.

evidence.title: Kisese II & Mumba (Northern Tanzania): Holocene LSA & pastoral sequence
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon chronology across ostrich eggshell beads and backed-microlith horizons in the Kondoa/Eyasi escarpment.
evidence.summary: Deeply dated interior Tanzanian shelters linking late Pleistocene/Holocene microlithic hunter-gatherers, rock-painting landscapes, and the transition to Pastoral Neolithic domestic herds.
evidence.limits: Shelters aggregate repeated intermittent camps across broad escarpment landscapes.

evidence.title: Matara / Metera (Senafe Highlands, Eritrea): Pre-Aksumite & Aksumite corridor town
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated stone multi-room elite mansions, Sabaic-Ge’ez monumental hawelti stela, Christian basilicas, and coinage.
evidence.summary: Strategic Eritrean plateau town connecting Aksum’s northern highland core with Red Sea port Adulis through monumental villas, indigenous highland pottery, and early Christian architecture.
evidence.limits: Fieldwork published chiefly from mid-twentieth-century excavation seasons awaits new AMS sequences.

evidence.title: Toteng & Ngamiland (Northwest Botswana): Early cattle & sheep in the Kalahari Basin
evidence.dateLabel: c. 100 BCE–700 CE (Bambata pottery & early livestock)
evidence.dateBasis: Directly dated livestock bone elements, palaeoproteomics (ZooMS), and Bambata-associated herder layers along Lake Ngami outlets.
evidence.summary: Early southern Kalahari-fringe pastoral contexts preserving directly dated cattle and domestic sheep bones before large Early Iron Age farming towns consolidated across the region.
evidence.limits: Bone fragmentation makes morphological vs. biomolecular identification essential to distinguish small bovids from wild game.

evidence.title: Little Muck & Skirbeek Shelters (Shashe-Limpopo): Forager–Farmer exchange
evidence.dateLabel: c. 100–1000 CE (Terminal LSA to Zhizo–K2 interaction)
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated rockshelter sequences, worked bone and hide-scraping suites, glass beads, and radiocarbon dates upstream/downstream of Mapungubwe.
evidence.summary: Illustrates active first-millennium economic exchange and shifting autonomy between Later Stone Age hunter-gatherers and arriving Early Iron Age Zhizo/Leopard’s Kopje farmers in the Limpopo corridor.
evidence.limits: Shelter deposits preserve small-scale craft and foraging toolkits alongside traded farming goods.

evidence.title: Sehonghong & Maloti-Drakensberg (Lesotho/SA): Highland hunter-gatherers & dairy uptake
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified rockshelter excavations, ancient faunal DNA, painted rock-art shelters, and lipid-residue dairying dates in highland Lesotho.
evidence.summary: High-altitude Drakensberg rock shelters sustain rich Holocene hunting-and-gathering lifeways, rock painting, and eventual adoption of milk-vessel use alongside lowland herder–farmer exchange in the first millennium CE.
evidence.limits: Mountain snows often concentrated occupations into seasonal warm-month highland visits.

evidence.title: Spoegrivier & Namaqualand (West Cape, SA): Earliest dated southern sheep via proteomic ID
evidence.dateBasis: Combined AMS radiocarbon determinations and ZooMS collagen-peptide palaeoproteomics confirming domestic Ovis aries.
evidence.summary: Direct biomolecular identification confirms domesticated fat-tailed sheep reached the Atlantic west coast of South Africa by roughly 2,000 years ago along pastoral networks well south of arriving farming towns.
evidence.limits: Represents sporadic early pastoral stock amidst continuing coastal marine foraging.

evidence.title: Karoo & Southern Interior: Terminal LSA forager–pastoralist frontier before 1000 CE
evidence.dateBasis: Compiled Southern African Radiocarbon Database site distributions alongside multi-proxy archaeological-linguistic reviews.
evidence.summary: Maps arid-interior Wilton lithic campsites persisting for millennia before uneven pastoral herding, thin-walled lugged pottery, and eastern Bantu-speaking iron farmers reshaped regional frontiers.
evidence.limits: Open surface scatters across the Karoo require shelter-based anchor stratigraphies.

evidence.title: Ndondondwane & KwaGandaganda (KwaZulu-Natal): Early Iron Age Thukela villages
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated river-valley central cattle-byre plazas, ivory-carving debris, iron-smelting furnaces, and charcoal wood-selection profiles.
evidence.summary: Early Iron Age farming towns along the Thukela and Mngeni rivers organized spatial hierarchies around central ritual/metallurgical zones, cattle pens, ivory bracelet workshops, and sorghum/millet fields.
evidence.limits: Subtropical valley erosion leaves truncated house floors outside mounded midden pits.

evidence.title: Matobo Hills (SW Zimbabwe): Holocene rock shelters & Bambata horizons
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified granite-boulder cave sequences (Pomongwe, Bambata, Nswatugi) and UNESCO Matobo painted shelter documentation.
evidence.summary: Granite kopjes across Matobo preserve dense Wilton microlithic occupations, painted kudu/giraffe ritual panels, and upper Bambata-pottery layers registering early herder–forager interactions north of the Limpopo.
evidence.limits: Stratigraphic mixing in historic Bambata trench excavations remains a focus of chronological review.

evidence.title: Kalundu Mound (Batoka Plateau, Zambia): Early Iron Age village economy
evidence.dateBasis: Re-analyzed radiocarbon chronology, fauna, and deep Early Iron Age village mound stratigraphy in southern Zambia.
evidence.summary: Documents early farming transition from wild hunting toward larger-scale cattle and caprine husbandry, sorghum/cowpea cultivation, and regional copper exchange north of the Zambezi.
evidence.limits: Mid-twentieth-century excavation volumes limit fine-grained micro-stratigraphic resolution.

evidence.title: Chibuene (Vilankulo Coast, Mozambique): Earliest southern Indian Ocean port
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified coastal sand-dune trading station with Zhizo-series glass beads, Nishapur/Siraf glazed wares, and local Gokomere-Zhizo pottery.
evidence.summary: Opened southern Mozambique’s Bazaruto channel to Persian Gulf and Swahili monsoon merchants by the seventh–eighth centuries CE, channeling imported glass beads inland to Zhizo and early Limpopo Valley capitals.
evidence.limits: Active coastal dune erosion threatens basal first-millennium occupation layers.

evidence.title: Lotshitshi (Southern Okavango Delta Margin): LSA–Bambata–Early Iron Age shift
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated delta-margin village deposits paired with archaeobotanical wood/seed analyses across Kalahari–Okavango wetlands.
evidence.summary: Preserves Bambata pottery and mixed wetland foraging transitioning smoothly into Early Iron Age agropastoral settlements sharing pearl millet, livestock, and copper-iron tools across northern Botswana.
evidence.limits: Sandy wetland stratigraphy blurs subtle micro-lenses between intermittent flood seasons.

evidence.title: Lakaton’i Anja & Velondriake (Madagascar): Pre-urban foraging & colonization debates
evidence.dateLabel: c. 2000 BCE–800 CE (Debated OSL vs. 1st-millennium CE settlement)
evidence.dateBasis: Paired OSL/AMS age reassessments at Lakaton’i Anja in northern Madagascar and shell-midden excavations along southwest Velondriake reefs.
evidence.summary: Evaluates disputed mid-Holocene micro-blade claims vs. firmer late first-millennium CE coastal foraging and marine shell exploitation at the threshold of Madagascar’s settled Bantu–Austronesian societies.
evidence.limits: Mixed sandstone shelter sands yield wide OSL vs. AMS uncertainties that keep pre-1st-millennium occupation hotly debated.

evidence.title: Sandrakatsy & Coastal Madagascar: Early villages, ironworking & mixed crops
evidence.dateBasis: Flotation phytolith/macrobotanical assays and early smelting/pottery horizons across northeastern coastal valleys.
evidence.summary: Early coastal villages mastered iron metallurgy and carved chloritic schist vessels while integrating Asian rice, mung bean, and yam with African/Malagasy coastal subsistence before larger entrepôts like Mahilaka rose.
evidence.limits: Humid coastal soils degrade bone and uncarbonized wood rapidly outside burned lenses.

evidence.title: Nasera Rockshelter (Serengeti Plains, Tanzania): Terminal LSA & Lemuta sequence
evidence.dateBasis: New excavations and backed-microlith / Kansyore-boundary dating across the Serengeti inselberg floor.
evidence.summary: Captures open savanna plains hunters producing specialized Lemuta LSA backed lithic assemblages and ostrich eggshell beads long before specialized pastoralists entered the Serengeti.
evidence.limits: Represents savanna mobile-camp seasons complementary to forested rift escarpment shelters.

evidence.title: Wadh Lang’o & Namundiri (Lake Victoria Basin): Holocene Kansyore fisher-foragers
evidence.dateBasis: AMS dates on fish-rich shell middens along the Nyanza Gulf and eastern Uganda lake margins prior to Urewe Iron Age layers.
evidence.summary: Semi-sedentary lacustrine communities around Lake Victoria harvested lungfish, tilapia, and Nile perch alongside distinctive stamped Kansyore ceramics for millennia before integrating sheep/cattle and Early Iron Age neighbors.
evidence.limits: Fluctuating lake-level shorelines periodically inundated lower fishing camps.

evidence.title: Southeastern Uganda Shelters (Kakapel–Victoria North): LSA to Early Iron syncretism
evidence.dateBasis: Multi-site LSA faunal sequences, Western Kansyore ceramics, and Transitional Urewe burial ritual studies.
evidence.summary: Illustrates long-term coexistence and ritual synthesis linking indigenous lakeshore Kansyore groups with arriving Urewe ironworkers across the northern Lake Victoria arc.
evidence.limits: Synthesis draws on uneven rockshelter vs. open mound coverage.

evidence.title: Shanga & Lamu Archipelago (Kenya): Timber mosques & northern Swahili genesis
evidence.dateBasis: Deep urban stratigraphy showing superposed posthole-timber and Porites coral mosques framed by Tana Tradition wares and silver/bead finds.
evidence.summary: Pate Island’s Shanga preserves an unbroken architectural sequence of coastal Muslim community life transitioning directly from local Bantu iron-and-fishing towns to coral-limestone urbanism before 1000 CE.
evidence.limits: Focuses on central sacred/market precincts within surrounding earthen neighborhoods.

evidence.title: Goda Buticha Cave (Dire Dawa, SE Ethiopia): Highland LSA Holocene sequence
evidence.dateBasis: AMS and OSL chronology through stratified volcanic-karst cave occupation layers rich in obsidian microliths and ostrich eggshell.
evidence.summary: Bridges the Horn of Africa’s Pleistocene–Holocene ecological boundary, documenting specialized highland obsidian microlithic toolkits and regional foraging adaptations preceding southern Red Sea/Harar pastoralism.
evidence.limits: Represents a single intensively dated southeastern escarpment cavern.

evidence.title: Wakrita (Djibouti) & Laas Geel (Somaliland): Early Horn pastoralism & rock art
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated Neolithic coastal-basalt sites in Gobaad (Wakrita) paired with high-resolution 3D recording of Laas Geel cattle shelter paintings.
evidence.summary: Monumental granite alcoves at Laas Geel and early pastoral settlements at Wakrita record indigenous cattle-and-caprine herding along the Gulf of Aden–Ethiopian rift rim centuries before urban kingdoms formed.
evidence.limits: Granite overhang pigments at Laas Geel lack direct AMS dates and are bracketed through regional Neolithic associations.

evidence.title: Harlaa & Western Somaliland Corridor (Eastern Ethiopia): Rise of Islamic caravan entrepôts
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated jewelry workshops, early coral-stone mosque foundations, Egyptian/Indian/Chinese imports, and borderland survey ceramics.
evidence.summary: Traces eastern Ethiopia’s cosmopolitan interior network linking Red Sea port Zeila with highland agriculturalists, shell/glass-bead craftspeople, and early Muslim mercantile towns.
evidence.limits: Early basal first-millennium strata beneath the stone town remain spatially restricted relative to twelfth–fourteenth-century levels.

evidence.title: Molokwane, Kaditshwene & Marothodi (North West, SA): Sotho-Tswana stone-walled towns
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon dates, ceramic sequences, GIS wall mapping and Tlokwa/Hurutshe/Kwena historical correlations across western Highveld mega-settlements.
evidence.summary: Extensive dry-stone bilobial residential and central cattle enclosures formed aggregated capitals of Kwena, Hurutshe and Tlokwa Tswana polities before early nineteenth-century regional upheavals.
evidence.limits: Dense settlement spans short overlapping political cycles; absolute population estimates from enclosure counts remain debated.

evidence.title: Suikerbosrand & Seoke (Gauteng/SE Botswana): Highveld & Kalahari-margin stone enclosures
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated stone-walled compound stratigraphies, pXRF soil chemistry and ceramic typologies across Suikerbosrand and Ngwaketse-area Seoke.
evidence.summary: Traces southern Highveld and southeastern Botswana agropastoralist households organizing grain storage, ironworking and livestock pens within clustered stone perimeter walls.
evidence.limits: Soil chemistry signals from kraal middens vary across eroded shallow hillslope soils.

evidence.title: uMgungundlovu, Ondini & Zulu amaKhanda Capitals (KwaZulu-Natal)
evidence.dateBasis: Historical archaeology of circular royal-military capitals (amakhanda) in the White Mfolozi / Makhosini Valley combined with nineteenth-century accounts.
evidence.summary: Excavations at royal amakhanda such as KwaBulawayo, uMgungundlovu and Ondini reveal planned concentric timber-and-thatch barracks, central parade grounds, cattle kraals and craft workshops at the heart of the Zulu Kingdom.
evidence.limits: Sequential capitals were intentionally burned and rebuilt upon dynastic transitions or imperial war.

evidence.title: Table Bay, Cobern Street & Robben Island (Western Cape): Maritime hub & Indian Ocean slavery
evidence.dateLabel: 1647–1834 CE (VOC wreck of Haarlem through Emancipation)
evidence.dateBasis: Underwater shipwreck archaeology in Table Bay, multi-isotope bioarchaeology of Cape Town burial grounds and VOC/British archival inventories.
evidence.summary: Following the 1647 Haarlem wreck and 1652 VOC provisioning post, Cape Town transformed indigenous Khoekhoe pastures into an oceanic chokepoint whose Cobern Street and Green Point burials preserve isotopic evidence of people forcibly brought from East Africa, Madagascar and South/Southeast Asia.
evidence.limits: Documentary ledgers undercount informal burials and indigenous seasonal camps around Table Valley.

evidence.title: Cederberg, Hanglip & Maloti-Drakensberg Contact Rock Art: Colonial resistance & continuity
evidence.dateBasis: Historical rock-art depictions of wagons, horses and ships paired with refuge shelter archaeology and Khoe-San descendant population genomics.
evidence.summary: Mountains across the Western Cape and Maloti-Drakensberg sheltered both runaway enslaved people (maroons) and mobile San/Khoekhoe groups whose late painted panels document horses, firearms, wagons and ritual resistance.
evidence.limits: Precise calendar dates for late colonial rock paintings rest largely on diagnostic depicted motifs.

evidence.title: Danamombe (Dhlodhlo) & Naletale (Central Zimbabwe): Rozvi Changamire capitals
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified Khami-phase stone platforms, imported porcelain/glass assemblages and historical records of the Changamire Rozvi state.
evidence.summary: Elaborately decorated dry-stone terraced platforms with chevron, herringbone and check patterns anchored the political, metallurgical and long-distance trade network of the Rozvi confederacy in south-central Zimbabwe.
evidence.limits: Antique relic-hunting in the nineteenth century disturbed upper aristocratic platform deposits.

evidence.title: Zvongombe, Baranda & Mutapa State (Northern Zimbabwe): Goldfields & Zambezi trade feiras
evidence.dateBasis: Zimbabwe-tradition stone loops at Zvongombe, Baranda market surveys and Portuguese-Mutapa treaty records.
evidence.summary: Shift of political hegemony from Great Zimbabwe toward northern Zambezia linked plateau alluvial gold extraction and dry-stone court centres with Afro-Portuguese trade fairs at Baranda and the Zambezi.
evidence.limits: Acidic savanna soils limit faunal preservation across several northern Mazowe Valley surveys.

evidence.title: Nyanga Terraces & Pit Structures (Eastern Highlands, Zimbabwe): Montane agro-engineering
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon dating, LiDAR/field mapping of dry-stone agricultural terraces, water furrows and sunken stock-pen compounds across ~7,000 sq km.
evidence.summary: Eastern Zimbabwe mountain slopes preserve thousands of kilometres of contoured stone field terraces, irrigated ridges and sunken homestead pits sustaining intensive cultivation and small-livestock herding.
evidence.limits: Terrace abandonment phases span several centuries cleanly separated only where pottery and charcoal co-occur.

evidence.title: Ingombe Ilede (Middle Zambezi, Zambia): Copper-cross ingot & gold trading cemetery
evidence.dateBasis: Direct AMS radiocarbon redating and compositional studies of flanged Katanga/Zambian copper croisettes, gold beads, iron gongs and Indian Ocean textiles.
evidence.summary: Hilltop cemetery on the Zambezi confluence whose richly furnished burials connect Copperbelt metallurgy, Zimbabwe Plateau goldworking and Swahili-coast glass beads along the Zambezi corridor.
evidence.limits: Kariba Dam construction limited rescue excavations prior to inundation of adjacent river flats.

evidence.title: Ilha de Moçambique (Nampula Coast): Swahili entrepôt to Lusophone Indian Ocean port
evidence.dateBasis: Comparative East African island archaeology, coral-rag urban stratigraphy, Fortaleza São Sebastião architecture and Indian Ocean maritime archives.
evidence.summary: Originally a Swahili-speaking Makua coastal town exporting ivory and interior gold, the limestone island became Portugal’s principal East African naval and commercial base on the Carreira da Índia until 1898.
evidence.limits: Continuous colonial and modern urban occupation obscures sub-surface pre-1500 timber horizons.

evidence.title: Vohemar (Iharana) & Teniky (Madagascar): Chlorite-schist trade & rock-cut architecture
evidence.dateBasis: Raman glass-bead spectroscopy and burial excavations at Vohemar paired with recent cliff-carved architecture dating at Teniky in Isalo.
evidence.summary: Northeast coast workshops exported turned green chlorite-schist vessels toward Swahili ports while Teniky in southern Madagascar’s Isalo sandstone massif preserves unusual rock-cut niches and terraces pointing to early long-distance Indian Ocean networks.
evidence.limits: Early twentieth-century looting of Vohemar tombs severed grave-goods associations in many lots.

evidence.title: Le Morne Brabant & Bois Marchand (Mauritius): Mascarene maroonage & Indian Ocean diasporas
evidence.dateBasis: Isotopic bioarchaeology of Bois Marchand and Le Morne cemeteries, upland maroon cave surveys and colonial plantation/indenture records.
evidence.summary: Settled only in the early modern era, Mauritius records how enslaved Africans and Malagasy maroons forged mountain refuges on Le Morne basalt cliffs, followed after 1834 abolition by massive South Asian indentured migration.
evidence.limits: Acidic basaltic soils and tropical cyclones preserve few perishable maroon campsite structures.

evidence.title: Mombasa (Fort Jesus) & Lamu Old Town (Kenya): Living Swahili stone towns & Red Sea–Omani shifts
evidence.dateBasis: Swahili urban stratigraphic sequences, Lamu coral-rag domestic architecture and the 1593–1698–19th century Fort Jesus citadel.
evidence.summary: Compacted coral-stone Swahili towns at Lamu and Pate flourished alongside Mombasa’s contested deep-water harbour, where Portuguese Fort Jesus (1593) fell to a 33-month Omani–Swahili siege in 1698 before Busaidi maritime integration.
evidence.limits: Living townscapes at Lamu and Old Town Mombasa restrict deep open-area trenching beneath standing stone houses.

evidence.title: Zanzibar Stone Town & Unguja (Tanzania): Swahili ceramics & 19th-century Busaidi entrepôt
evidence.dateBasis: Local Tana/Swahili ceramic studies, Stone Town heritage fabric and nineteenth-century Omani sultanate, clove-plantation and abolition archives.
evidence.summary: Ceramic workshops and enslaved/migrant neighbourhood archaeology trace Unguja from medieval fishing and coral-stone villages into the nineteenth-century seat of the Busaidi Sultanate linking East African ivory and clove plantations to Mumbai, Muscat and Europe.
evidence.limits: Dense nineteenth-century masonry overprints earlier mud-and-thatch quarters of Shangani and Malindi.

evidence.title: Thimlich Ohinga & Gunda-Buche Enclosures (Lake Victoria Basin, Kenya): Stone-walled compounds
evidence.dateBasis: Spatial GIS analysis, mortarless basalt-block wall typology and oral historical synthesis across Migori and western Kenya.
evidence.summary: More than 500 dry-stone enclosures (ohinga / gunda-buche) in southwestern Kenya protected clustered livestock kraals, grain stores and lineage homesteads amid Lake Victoria agropastoral migrations.
evidence.limits: Minimal organic carbon trapped within unmortared basalt walls leaves early construction horizons poorly dated.

evidence.title: Munsa, Kibiro Salt Works & Kasubi Tombs (Uganda): Great Lakes capitals & resource states
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon-dated earthwork ditches at Munsa, millennia-deep brining ash mounds at Lake Albert Kibiro and Buganda capital/Kasubi surveys.
evidence.summary: Great Lakes political centralization rested on strategic salt springs on Lake Albert (Kibiro), cattle/iron earthworks (Munsa), and later mobile royal capitals (kibuga) and monumental barkcloth-and-thatch mausolea of Buganda (Kasubi).
evidence.limits: Dense tropical vegetation and nineteenth-century capital relocations complicate stratigraphic correlation across kingdoms.

evidence.title: Harar Jugol, Ifat & Aw-Barkhadle (Ethiopia/Somaliland): Islamic escarpment towns & caravan ports
evidence.dateBasis: Excavations at Ifat/Nora/Aw-Barkhadle, Somaliland long-distance trade surveys and standing mosques/jugol walls at Harar prior to 1887 incorporation.
evidence.summary: Linking the Chercher/Harar highlands to Berbera and Zeila on the Gulf of Aden, the Sultanates of Shoa, Ifat, Adal and the walled Emirate of Harar integrated coffee, khat, ivory and textile commerce with Islamic scholarship.
evidence.limits: Regional medieval borderland surveys remain patchy across active pastoral zones in eastern Ogaden and Somaliland.

evidence.title: Tiya Carved Stelae & Konso Walled Terraces (Central/Southern Ethiopia)
evidence.dateBasis: Burial excavations beneath Gurage-zone sword-carved megaliths at Tiya and indigenous terrace-and-walled-town (paleta) heritage studies in Konso.
evidence.summary: Beyond northern Christian and eastern Islamic states, central and southern Ethiopian highland societies erected figurative funerary stelae cemeteries (Tiya) and engineered multi-century dry-stone terraced towns and water-retention ponds (Konso).
evidence.limits: Several Ethiopian stelae fields remain undated beyond broad twelfth-to-fourteenth-century cemetery determinations.

evidence.title: Kondoa & Kisese II Rock-Art Sites (Tanzania): Terminal Pleistocene ochre to late white-paste art
evidence.dateLabel: c. 15,000 BCE–1500 CE (Ochre >30 ka to late paintings)
evidence.dateBasis: Direct AMS ostrich-eggshell bead sequences and red ochre pencils at Kisese II coupled with superposed Kondoa granite-shelter panels (UNESCO WHC 1183).
evidence.summary: Connects Terminal Pleistocene hunter-gatherer red ochre traditions at Kisese II with millennia of naturalistic Sandawe-affiliated hunting paintings and late agro-pastoralist white symbolic finger art across central Tanzania.
evidence.limits: Lack of organic binders in mineral red hematites hinders direct radiocarbon dating of individual animal motifs.

evidence.title: Twyfelfontein / ǀUi-ǁAes & Doro !Nawas (Namibia): Desert spring rock engravings & pastoral transition
evidence.dateBasis: >2,500 sandstone petroglyphs depicting giraffe, rhino, human footprints and shamanic transformations plus Erongo–Doro !Nawas ochre sourcing (UNESCO WHC 1255).
evidence.summary: Marks long-term ritual congregation around dependable Kunene desert springs where LSA hunter-gatherers and later Damara–Khoe sheep herders engraved tracks and rain-making imagery.
evidence.limits: Sandstone varnish cation-ratio estimates retain wide uncertainty bars without buried petroglyph talus dates.

evidence.title: Kakapel Shelter (Western Kenya) & Singida Outcrops: Geometric, cattle & rainmaking granite panels
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified shelter sequences and multi-style superpositions linking Batwa forager geometric art with incoming Nilotic and Bantu cattle symbols.
evidence.summary: Documents multi-ethnic cultural frontiers north and south of Lake Victoria–Singida through geometric concentric circles, humpbacked cattle depictions and sacred cupule–gong granite shelters.
evidence.limits: Exposed tropical shelter surfaces suffer localized lichen growth and seasonal smoke blackening.

waves.title: Swahili Coast & Western Indian Ocean maritime network
waves.summary: Monsoon navigation connected Swahili coral-stone port towns from Lamu and Zanzibar through Kilwa to Comoros and northwest Madagascar, carrying hinterland gold, ivory, timber, rock crystal, Asian rice, glass beads, and Chinese porcelain.
waves.limits: Schematic maritime arc linking excavated coastal port towns rather than individual sailing tracks.

waves.title: Southern Zambezia–Zimbabwe Plateau–Swahili Indian Ocean Corridor (c. 1000–1850 CE)
waves.dateBasis: Sourced interior copper ingots, reef gold, ivory, Indo-Pacific glass beads and Chinese porcelains linking plateau capitals to Sofala, Ilha de Moçambique and Kilwa.
waves.summary: Schematic interior-to-coast trade corridor illustrating flows of gold, ivory and Katanga/Zambezi copper toward Sofala, Chibuene and northern Swahili stone-town ports.
waves.limits: Lines connect researched centres along variable seasonal river and plateau trails, not fixed surveyed highways.
